thread:
kai: Heads-up, ran k-fold (5) onboarding for launchpadv0 on our three benchmarks + a short-query split. seeing high variance on long-tail cohorts.

jules: paste the summary numbers?

kai: top-level: msmarco R@1 mean=0.468 (std=0.007), R@5 mean=0.701. wiki-snips R@1=0.586. product-holdout overall R@1=0.412 but short-query cohort R@1=0.495 and long-tail (sku-heavy) R@1=0.351.

anya: that's a pretty big cohort gap. how does that compare to our baseline heron-v2?

kai: heron-v2 kfold: msmarco R@1 mean=0.492 (std=0.004), product overall R@1=0.458, short-query R@1=0.509, long-tail R@1=0.417. so launchpad loses ~0.06 on long-tail absolute.

sam: did you run clustering / density checks? maybe representation collapse for rare tokens.

kai: ran UMAP + HDBSCAN on product vectors. cluster count down ~18% vs baseline, a lot of "misc" noise cluster points. avg cluster size variance higher. attached kNN failure dump for top 200 failing queries.

jules: quantitative diagnostic? any per-token norm shifts?

kai: yes: mean embedding norm (fp32) launchpad = 2.11, heron = 1.98. but for rare-token skus launchpad norms are ~2.5 with higher dispersion. after L2-normalization (post) long-tail R@1 improved +0.023 but still below baseline.

anya: interesting. what about quantized variants? int4 / int8?

kai: int8-ptq delta vs fp32: long-tail R@1 -0.012. int4-é (we tried per-channel int4) shows -0.035 but memory wins are large. for quick tests, int8 with l2 norm gives best cost/quality trade.

sam: can you drop repro commands & paths? i want to run the same kfold.

kai: sure:
```
python eval_embed.py --model launchpadv0 --variant fp32 --datasets msmarco,wiki-snips,product-holdout --kfold 5 --seed 42 --save-knn /tmp/launchpad_kfold/
python eval_embed.py --model launchpadv0 --variant int8-ptq --datasets product-holdout --normalize l2 --split short,long-tail
```

eval-bot: automated compare: launchpadv0 vs heron-v2 (product-holdout long-tail): R@1 delta -0.066 (level=high), silhouette delta -0.05 (level=medium). Recommendation: triage long-tail failure cohort. Artifacts: https://redwood-internal/s3/evals/launchpadv0/1769901110/index.html

jules: next steps proposal: 1) run a small id-contrastive fine-tune on 1M product pairs (derek/systems to schedule), 2) try temperature scaling in loss or a margin tweak during fine-tune, 3) include per-example norm-clipping as preprocessing, 4) stage canary route for non-product traffic. owners?

anya: i'll own 4) (routing + metrics). kai will own 2) & 3). sam can coordinate 1) with ML infra.

kai: thanks. i'll upload the failing kNN CSV + a short notebook showing UMAP & cluster summaries. will re-run after 2) & 3) and post deltas. :rocket:

eval-bot: upload complete: s3://redwood-internal/evals/launchpadv0/1769901110/knn_failures.csv

sam: perfect. let's reconvene after the id-ft run. aim for long-tail R@1 +0.03 to be in baseline parity. :thumbsup:
